The suspect, Courtney Mori, was taken into custody after traveling through private property for approximately a quarterman. Mile. During the pursuit, Mori crashed into an old concrete bridge abutment, traveling about 21 miles per hour just before impact with the accelerator pressed, and no braking applied. The vehicle sustained damage to the front driver's side fender, push bumper and hood, and was subsequently towed from the scene. The officer who was bitten received treatment at Trinity Hospital. Mori was charged with assaulting a police officer, unlawful driving away fleeing a police officer and malicious destruction of police property. Mori was sentenced to one to three years of probation, with fees totaling approximately $1,234. Several times throughout the chase, the training officer instructs the driver to scrub. In emergency vehicle operations, drivers are trained to break in a straight line before entering a curve. Tires achieve maximum traction when focused on a single task at a time. Therefore, troopers break before the turn, navigate through the curve, and then accelerate hard after exiting, maximizing both control and safety.
